title: Recommendation generator v0: heuristics for cache hit-rate improvement (fragmentation/diversity/policy mismatches)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Build recommendation generator v0 (heuristics) that consumes v2 prefix/KV cache telemetry aggregates and emits ranked, actionable “increase cache hit-rate” recommendations with evidence links. This is the MVP engine used by Optimize/Console recommendations feed.

Goal
- Turn cache telemetry into customer-facing (and internal) actions that measurably improve cache effectiveness.
- Focus on three initial detectors:
  1) Routing fragmentation (requests with similar prefixes split across many routes/models/versions/regions)
  2) Prompt prefix diversity (too many distinct prefixes / low reuse preventing cache hits)
  3) Cache policy mismatches (workload would benefit from caching but cache disabled/too-small TTL/evictions dominating)

Non-goals (this ticket)
- ML-based recommendation ranking or clustering beyond simple hashing/bucketing.
- Major cache algorithm changes in runtime.
- Perfect precision; we prioritize conservative guardrails + high-signal evidence.

Inputs (expected from telemetry pipeline)
- Aggregated cache metrics by {tenant, deployment_mode, region, route_id (or route_group), model_id, model_version} with bounded cardinality.
- Metrics: hit_rate, hit_bytes, miss_bytes, saved_prefill_ms, cacheable_prompt_ratio, evictions, inserts, lookup_count, partial_hit_rate (if available).
- Optional: prefix_bucket_id or “normalized_prefix_hash” bucket counts (NOT raw prefixes).

Outputs
- A list of recommendation records per tenant (and optionally per route group) with:
  - type (fragmentation | prefix_diversity | policy_mismatch)
  - severity (info | warn | critical)
  - title + short action text
  - ranked score (0-100)
  - evidence links (dashboards + query deep links) and evidence snippets (top contributing segments)
  - suppression key + TTL to avoid spamming the same rec

Where it runs
- Batch job (hourly) in Optimize backend worker (preferred) OR analytics job writing into recommendations table used by Console.
- Must align with API contract being finalized in PM-912 + backend work in PR #18488.

Implementation sketch
- Compute tenant-level baselines: hit_rate, saved_prefill_ms/request, cacheable_prompt_ratio.
- Detector A: routing fragmentation
  - Heuristic: identify top N “prefix bucket” cohorts (or proxy: requests with high cacheable_prompt_ratio) where traffic is distributed across >K distinct {route_id/model_version/region} with low per-segment hit_rate.
  - Recommend: “Pin model version” / “reduce route splits” / “consolidate routing policy” for these cohorts.
- Detector B: prompt prefix diversity
  - Heuristic: cacheable_prompt_ratio high but hit_rate low AND prefix bucket entropy high (or unique_bucket_count high / reuse low).
  - Recommend: prompt normalization (stable headers/system prompts), template factoring, avoiding per-request random salts, consistent tool formatting.
- Detector C: cache policy mismatches
  - Heuristic: cacheable_prompt_ratio high but inserts low OR evictions high with low saved_prefill_ms; or cache disabled for a route with heavy prefill costs.
  - Recommend: enable caching for specific routes, adjust TTL/size, align cache namespace with model version.

Guardrails
- Never recommend changes when data quality flags are present (sampling too low, cardinality guardrails dropping tags, known misclassification period).
- Require minimum traffic threshold per tenant/route group (e.g., >= 10k requests/day or >= 50M tokens/day; to be tuned).
- Evidence must cite time window + show top contributing breakdowns (e.g., “60% of cacheable requests split across 7 model versions”).

Evidence links
- Use dashboards defined in ENG-4817 (cache hit-rate dashboards). Evidence links should be stable and tenant-scoped (no raw IDs in URL when avoidable).
acceptance_criteria: Generates at least 3 recommendation types: routing fragmentation, prompt prefix diversity, cache policy mismatch.
Each recommendation includes: type, severity, score, short action text, and >=1 evidence link to dashboards (tenant-scoped).
Conservative thresholds + minimum traffic filters to avoid noisy output for small tenants/routes.
Deduping/suppression implemented (same tenant+type+scope does not re-emit more than once per 24h unless severity increases).
Unit tests with synthetic fixtures cover: (a) fragmentation scenario, (b) high diversity scenario, (c) eviction/policy mismatch scenario, (d) low-traffic/no-data scenario => emits nothing.
Does not require raw prompt content; uses only hashed/bucketed aggregates (privacy-safe).
End-to-end integration verified with recommendations feed API (PM-912 / PR #18488): Console can fetch and render records.
Runbook note added for how to interpret recommendations + how to disable generator if it becomes noisy (link to ENG-4820).
implementation_notes:
Ranking/Scoring (v0)
- Score = weighted sum of: estimated_savings (normalized saved_prefill_ms potential), confidence (traffic volume + stability), and actionability (clear next step).
- Severity mapping:
  - critical: expected_savings high AND confidence high
  - warn: moderate savings/confidence
  - info: low savings or exploratory

Suggested thresholds (initial; tune with SRE/Telemetry)
- Min traffic per scope: >= 2k requests/6h OR >= 5M tokens/6h.
- Fragmentation:
  - top cohort traffic share >= 0.25 AND distinct_segments >= 4 AND median hit_rate across segments < 0.2
- Diversity:
  - cacheable_prompt_ratio >= 0.6 AND hit_rate <= 0.15 AND unique_prefix_buckets_per_1k_reqs >= X (requires pipeline field)
- Policy mismatch:
  - cacheable_prompt_ratio >= 0.6 AND (inserts/lookup_count) < 0.05 OR evictions/inserts > 0.5

Data quality gating
- Check pipeline-provided quality flags (sampling_rate, dropped_tag_rate, schema_version).
- If schema_version < v2 or dropped_tag_rate above threshold => emit no recs and log reason.

Storage
- Write into recommendations table introduced in Optimize/Console backend (PR #18488). Include suppression_key and emitted_at.

Open questions
- Do we want “scope” to be tenant-only for MVP, or tenant+route_group? My suggestion: emit both but prefer tenant-level unless route_group signal is strong.
- For Private deployments, attribution fields may be partial; should emit only tenant-level recs when route_id/model_version missing.
comments: 2025-02-11 (Aditya Rao): Please keep the recommendation copy short and action-oriented. For MVP we need: title, 1-2 bullets for “Why this is happening”, and 1 bullet for “What to do next”. Evidence links are mandatory; evidence snippets are strongly preferred.

2025-02-12 (Nadia Rahman): Pipeline can provide unique_prefix_bucket_count and prefix_bucket_entropy only if we’re comfortable with an extra aggregate keyed by (tenant, route_group, model_version, region). We should confirm cardinality budget impact with Thomas before relying on entropy; otherwise we can proxy with cacheable_prompt_ratio + low hit_rate + high miss_bytes.

2025-02-13 (Rafael Mendes): Please add noise controls. Oncall can’t handle a flood of recs if a region is rolling out v2 telemetry and temporarily misreports hit_rate. Require schema_version=v2 + min sampling window before emitting anything.
2025-02-14 (Hassan Mirza): I’ll implement gating on schema_version and a 12h warmup after first-seen v2 telemetry per tenant. Also adding a suppression key per (tenant,type,scope) with 24h TTL.

2025-02-18 (Mina Haddad): For fragmentation, consider splitting model_version vs region separately. We’ve seen “fragmentation” that’s actually intended multi-region routing for latency. We should prefer recommending model_version pinning (within region) over “reduce regions” unless cross-region traffic share is high and hit savings is obvious.

2025-02-20 (Logan Wright): +1. Also please use route_group rather than route_id where possible (align with ADR-027) to avoid cardinality blowups. If route_group is missing, fall back to tenant-level only.

2025-02-24 (Hassan Mirza): PR #18502 is up with detectors A/B and scaffolding for C. Still blocked on final pipeline field names for entropy/unique buckets; for now it uses a proxy metric and logs a TODO when those fields are absent.
status_updates: 2025-02-14: Drafted detector logic + gating rules; aligned with PM on required output fields and evidence links.
2025-02-19: Implemented fragmentation and diversity detectors behind feature flag optimize.cache_recs_v0; added suppression/deduping.
2025-02-24: Opened PR #18502; unit tests added with synthetic fixtures. Next: policy mismatch detector + integrate dashboard deep links once ENG-4817 queries are finalized.
risks: If prefix diversity signal relies on entropy fields not available in v2 aggregates, detector B may be noisy; mitigate by shipping as info severity until entropy available.
Misclassification of partial hits could skew hit_rate vs saved_prefill_ms; mitigate by gating on saved_prefill_ms consistency checks and known-issues window.
Private deployment attribution gaps may prevent scoped recs; mitigate by emitting only tenant-level recs when route/model metadata is absent.
